akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿قَدْراً﴾, and some read ﴿قَدَراً﴾; they are two dialectal variants.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ﴾: "الوُجْد" is means (ability); and some of the Arabs pronounce it with kasra in this sense. As for "الوَجْدُ", when you give the wāw a fatḥa, it is "love" (الحُبّ). In meaning — and Allah knows best — it is: "Lodge them where you dwell, from what you are able to afford" (أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُم مِمَّا تَقْدِرُون عليه).

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾: He made ﴿الأرْض﴾ a plurality, just as you say "هَلَكَ الشاةُ والبَعِيرُ" ("the sheep and the camel have perished") while you mean all the sheep and all the camels.*

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ﴾: what is meant is his nation, by the indication of what follows it, i.e. say to them: ﴿إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ﴾, i.e. you intend divorce, ﴿فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾ at its beginning, by the divorce being in a state of purity in which she has not been touched, because of his ﷺ explaining it so — narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim). ﴿وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ﴾ keep count of it, so that you may take back before it ends; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ﴾ obey Him in His command and His prohibition. ﴿لَا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخْرُجْنَ﴾ from them until their waiting period ends, ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾ fornication ﴿مُبَيَّنَةٍ﴾ — with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with kasra [مُبَيِّنَةٍ], i.e. made clear, or clear — then they go out for the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) to be carried out on them. ﴿وَتِلْكَ﴾ the things mentioned ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ لَا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ﴾ divorce ﴿أَمْرًا﴾: taking back, in the case where it was one or two.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ approach the end of their waiting period, ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ by taking them back ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ without causing harm, ﴿أَوْ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾: leave them until their waiting period ends, and do not harm them by taking them back. ﴿وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ over the taking back or the parting, ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهَادَةَ لِلَّهِ﴾, not for the one against whom or for whom testimony is given. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا﴾ from the distresses of this world and the Hereafter,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ﴾ it occurs to his mind. ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ in his affairs, ﴿فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ﴾ sufficient for him. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَالِغٌ أَمْرَهُ﴾ His intent — and in a reading [بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ], as a genitive construct (iḍāfa). ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ such as ease and hardship ﴿قَدْرًا﴾ an appointed time.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَاللَّائِي﴾, with hamza and yāʾ, and without yāʾ, in both places, ﴿يَئِسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ﴾ in the sense of menstruation ﴿مِنْ نِسَائِكُمْ إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ﴾ you are in doubt about their waiting period, ﴿فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ﴾ because of their youth: their waiting period is three months. Both cases concern women other than those whose husbands have died; as for them, their waiting period is what is in the verse «يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا». ﴿وَأُولَاتُ الْأَحْمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ﴾ the end of their waiting period, whether divorced or widowed, ﴿أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا﴾ in this world and the Hereafter.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ which is mentioned concerning the waiting period ﴿أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ His ruling ﴿أَنْزَلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ وَيُعْظِمْ لَهُ أَجْرًا﴾.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ﴾, i.e. the divorced women, ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُمْ﴾, i.e. some of your dwellings, ﴿مِنْ وُجْدِكُمْ﴾, i.e. your means: ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or badal (substitute) from what precedes it, with the preposition repeated and a muḍāf implied, i.e. the places of your means, not what is below them. ﴿وَلَا تُضَارُّوهُنَّ لِتُضَيِّقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ the dwellings, so that they are forced to leave, or (to give up) maintenance, and ransom themselves from you. ﴿وَإِنْ كُنَّ أُولَاتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنْفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّى يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ﴾ your children by them, ﴿فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ for the suckling, ﴿وَأْتَمِرُوا بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ and them ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ in a fair way concerning the children's right, by agreeing on a known wage for the suckling. ﴿وَإِنْ تَعَاسَرْتُمْ﴾ you make difficulties over the suckling, so the father refuses the wage and the mother refuses to do it, ﴿فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ﴾ for the father ﴿أُخْرَى﴾, and the mother is not compelled to suckle him.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ﴾ on the divorced women and the nursing women ﴿ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ وَمَنْ قُدِرَ﴾ restricted ﴿عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتَاهُ﴾ given him ﴿اللَّهُ﴾, according to his measure. ﴿لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا مَا آتَاهَا سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا﴾ — and He did make it, through the conquests.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ﴾: it is the kāf of jarr entering on أَيّ, in the sense of كَمْ; ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾, i.e. and many of the towns, ﴿عَتَتْ﴾ rebelled — meaning its people — ﴿عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهَا وَرُسُلِهِ فَحَاسَبْنَاهَا﴾ in the Hereafter — even though it has not come, because of the certainty of its occurrence — ﴿حِسَابًا شَدِيدًا وَعَذَّبْنَاهَا عَذَابًا نُكْرًا﴾, with sukūn on the kāf and with ḍamma: dreadful, and it is the punishment of the Fire.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَاقَتْ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهَا﴾ its punishment, ﴿وَكَانَ عَاقِبَةُ أَمْرِهَا خُسْرًا﴾ loss and destruction.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا﴾: repeating the threat is tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ possessors of intellects, ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of the one addressed (al-munādā), or an explication (bayān) of it. ﴿قَدْ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْرًا﴾: it is the Quran;

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿رَسُولًا﴾, i.e. Muhammad ﷺ: accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb, i.e. "and He sent"; ﴿يَتْلُوا عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيَّنَاتٍ﴾, with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with kasra [مُبَيِّنَاتٍ], as preceded, ﴿لِيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ after the coming of the Reminder and the Messenger ﴿مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ the disbelief they were in ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ the faith which took hold of them after disbelief. ﴿وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صَالِحًا يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ — and in a reading with nūn — ﴿جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقًا﴾: it is the provision of Paradise, whose bliss never ceases.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾, meaning seven earths; ﴿يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ﴾ the revelation ﴿بَيْنَهُنَّ﴾ between the heavens and the earth: Gabriel brings it down from the seventh heaven to the seventh earth; ﴿لِتَعْلَمُوا﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted (verb), i.e. He informed you of that creation and sending down, ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ «يا» is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ badal (substitute); ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿رَبَّكُمْ﴾ badal; ﴿لا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the wāw being its fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَلا يَخْرُجْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, and it is in the position of a jussive by the prohibitive «لا», the nūn being its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿أَنْ يَأْتِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; ﴿بِفاحِشَةٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective); ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ «[Translator's note: the source prints «مِنْ»; the word in the verse is «مَنْ».]»; ﴿يَتَعَدَّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to the Name of Majesty «[Translator's note: the quoted word is printed with a ḍamma in the source; in the verse it is «حُدُودَ», accusative.]»; ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective; ﴿قد ظَلَمَ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿نَفْسَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من», and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿تَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ﴾ «لعلّ», its noun being the Name of Majesty, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of «لعلّ»; ﴿بَعْدَ ذلِكَ﴾ an adverb of time, and a demonstrative in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa; ﴿أَمْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of «تدري», and the clause «تدري» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and «إذا» is an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَوْ فارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿وَأَشْهِدُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿ذَوَيْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ; ﴿عَدْلٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «ذوي»; ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿ذلِكُمْ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يُوعَظُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿مَنْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿كانَ﴾ «كان» and its latent (mustatir) noun; ﴿يُؤْمِنُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «كان», and the clause «كان» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من»; ﴿وَالْيَوْمِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الْآخِرِ﴾ a naʿt of «اليوم». ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent and the Name of Majesty the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يَجْعَلْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿مَخْرَجاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of «من», and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَيَرْزُقْهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يجعل», jussive (majzūm) like it, the hāʾ being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَحْتَسِبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Translator's note: the source prints «مِنْ»; the word in the verse is «مَنْ».]»; ﴿يَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of «من», and the clause «من..» is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ﴾ «إنّ», its noun and its khabar; ﴿أَمْرِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿قَدْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَاللَّائِي﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَئِسْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) «[Translator's note: so in the source; «يَئِسْنَ» is a past verb.]»; ﴿مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ﴾ «إن» is a conditional particle making the verb jussive, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); ﴿عدتهن ثَلاثَةُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); ﴿أَشْهُرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «اللائي», and the clause «اللائي..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ, and an imperfect verb in the jussive by «لم», the nūn being its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is omitted, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿أُولاتُ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْأَحْمالِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿أَجَلُهُنَّ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿أَنْ يَضَعْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the nūn of the feminine plural being its fāʿil; ﴿حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of «أجلهن», and the nominal clause «أجلهن..» is the khabar of «أولات». ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْراً﴾: its i'rab has been given before.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿ذلِكَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَنْزَلَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun making the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ; ﴿يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil being latent and the Name of Majesty the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يُكَفِّرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its fāʿil being latent; ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿سَيِّئاتِهِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من», and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَيُعْظِمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يكفر»; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿أَجْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿سَكَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿مِنْ وُجْدِكُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for His saying «من حيث»; ﴿وَلا تُضآرُّوهُنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil and the hāʾ its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لِتُضَيِّقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), the wāw being its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to the verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ both are attached to the verb as well. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ كُنَّ﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun; ﴿أُولاتِ حَمْلٍ﴾ its khabar (predicate), annexed to «حمل», and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿حَتَّى يَضَعْنَ﴾ «حتى» is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative by the implicit «أن» after «حتى», the nūn of the feminine plural being the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive governed by «حتى», and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to the verb; ﴿حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿أَرْضَعْنَ﴾ a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, the nūn of the feminine plural being its fāʿil; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is initial, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَآتُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective, and an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its first object; ﴿أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; ﴿وَأْتَمِرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb [and] its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿تَعاسَرْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the clause is initial, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَسَتُرْضِعُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿أُخْرى﴾ fāʿil.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿ذُو سَعَةٍ﴾ fāʿil (agent), annexed to «سعة», and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Translator's note: the source prints «مِنْ»; the word in the verse is «مَنْ».]»; ﴿قُدِرَ﴾ a passive past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿رِزْقُهُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿فَلْيُنْفِقْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām of command, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of «من», and the clause «من..» is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿آتاهُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ﴾ «لا» is negating, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; ﴿نَفْساً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿ما﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿آتاها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila of «ما», with no grammatical position. ﴿سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ﴾ the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position; ﴿بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to «عسر»; ﴿يُسْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿كَأَيِّنْ﴾ an allusive noun (ism kināya) meaning "many", indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿قَرْيَةٍ﴾ tamyīz (specification); ﴿عَتَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿عَنْ أَمْرِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَبِّها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَحاسَبْناها﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿حِساباً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿شَدِيداً﴾ a naʿt (adjective); ﴿وَعَذَّبْناها عَذاباً نُكْراً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَذاقَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿وَبالَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَمْرِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَكانَ عاقِبَةُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and «كان» and its noun; ﴿أَمْرِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خُسْراً﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿شَدِيداً﴾ a naʿt (adjective); ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil, the Name of Majesty being the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿يا أُولِي﴾ «يا» is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); ﴿الْأَلْبابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ badal (substitute); ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿ذِكْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb; ﴿يَتْلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولا»; ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿آياتِ اللَّهِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿مُبَيِّناتٍ﴾ a naʿt; ﴿لِيُخْرِجَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), the fāʿil being latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to «يتلو»; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «آمنوا»; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ﴾ both are attached to «يخرج»; ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ both are attached to «يخرج» as well. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مِنَ﴾ a conditional noun making the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Translator's note: the source prints «مِنَ»; the word in the verse is «مَنْ».]»; ﴿يُؤْمِنْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent; ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿وَيَعْمَلْ﴾ conjoined to «يؤمن»; ﴿صالِحاً﴾ the naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied form being «ويعمل عملا صالحا» (and does a righteous deed). ﴿يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent and the hāʾ the first object; ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «من», and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt; ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾ both are attached to «خالدين»; ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); ﴿أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil; ﴿لَهُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿رِزْقاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذي»; ﴿سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to «السموات»; ﴿وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «وخلق» (and He created); ﴿مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾ the mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb; ﴿يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَهُنَّ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿لِتَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), the wāw being its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to «خلق». ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ «أنّ» and its noun; ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both are attached to «قدير»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of «أنّ», and the interpreted maṣdar made from «أنّ» and what follows it is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of «تعلموا»; ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ «أنّ» and its noun; ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); ﴿أَحاطَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «أنّ», and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿عِلْماً﴾ tamyīz (specification).

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ) إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition, and the clause طلقتم النساء is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb. It is plural only because the call is directed to the Prophet together with his community, or because the word "the Prophet" is used while his community is meant. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He singled out the Prophet ﷺ in the call and made the address general, because the Prophet is the leader of his community and their exemplar, just as one says to the chief and elder of a people, "O so-and-so, do [pl.] such and such", out of regard for his precedence and to display his leadership with fine speech». The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); طلّقوهنّ is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Concerning what the lām is attached to there is great disagreement among the schools of the jurists, and the best thing to say about it is that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "facing, by divorcing them, the ʿidda (waiting period)", that is, the time in which they begin it. Al-Bayḍāwī's words are: «لعدتهنّ, i.e. at its time, which is the state of purity; for the lām with times and what resembles them is for timing. Whoever counts the ʿidda by menstrual periods — namely Abū Ḥanīfa — attaches the lām to something omitted such as "facing". Its apparent sense indicates that the ʿidda is by periods of purity, and that the divorce of a woman who observes the ʿidda by al-iqrār [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «الأقراء» "the quruʾ, the monthly periods"] should be in [a state of] purity, and that it is forbidden during menstruation, inasmuch as commanding a thing entails forbidding its opposite; but it does not indicate that it does not take effect, since a prohibition, when it is due to an external matter, does not entail invalidity».
Zāde, in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī, commented on these words, saying: «His saying "attaches the lām to something omitted", i.e. because he cannot make the lām one of timing, given the consensus that al-iṭlāq [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «الطلاق» "divorce"] during menstruation is prohibited; rather he attaches it to something omitted, indicated by the meaning of the speech, i.e. "divorce them facing their ʿidda", that is, heading towards it. When a woman is divorced in the state of purity preceding the first of her quruʾ, she has been divorced facing her ʿidda. What is meant is that they be divorced in a state of purity in which there has been no intercourse with them, and then be left until their ʿidda is over. He supported this with the reading فطلقوهنّ من قبل عدّتهنّ».
As for Abū Ḥayyān, he dealt with the subject at length and debated al-Zamakhsharī in an enjoyable discussion; this is the text of his words: «The lām is for timing, as in "I wrote it when one night remained of such-and-such month". Al-Zamakhsharī's supposition here of an omitted ḥāl, indicated by the meaning, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached — i.e. "facing their ʿidda" — is not good, because he supposed a specific governor, and the governor of an adverb or of a preposition and its genitive noun is not omitted when it is specific, but only when it is a general [notion of] being. If you said "Zayd is with you" or "in the house", meaning "laughing with you" or "laughing in the house", it would not be permissible. So attaching the lām to His saying فطلقوهنّ, and making it on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, is what is correct». By supposing the muḍāf, Abū Ḥayyān means "for the facing of their ʿidda". Abū al-Baqāʾ did not address what the lām is attached to. I have seen a comment of Ibn al-Munayyir, said in reply to al-Zamakhsharī, which we also cite below: «Al-Zamakhsharī compared the lām in it to the lām in your saying, when dating: "I came to him when one night remained of al-Muḥarram"; he means only that the ʿidda is by menstrual periods. All of this is partisanship for the school of Abū Ḥanīfa, that al-iqrāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, for «الأقراء»] are the menstrual periods, and he does not succeed in it. Our companions argued from the widely transmitted reading, and strengthened the indication with the irregular (shādhdha) one, that al-aqrāʾ are the periods of purity. The way of arguing from it for that is that Allah the Exalted made the ʿidda — even though it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) — an adverb (ẓarf) for the divorce that is commanded; and the Arabs often use maṣdars as adverbs, such as "the setting of the star" and "the arrival of the pilgrims". And if the ʿidda is an adverb for the commanded divorce, and its time is the state of purity by agreement, then al-ẓahr [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «الطهر» "purity"] is the ʿidda. The true parallel of the lām here is the lām in His saying "Would that I had sent ahead for my life", for he only wished that he had done some deed during his life».
(وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ) أحصوا is an imperative verb conjoined to the command before it, and العدّة is the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. keep track of the time in which the divorce took place, so that you may take [them] back before it ends, and so that you may know the period of maintenance and lodging, the lawfulness of marrying the divorced woman's sister, and similar matters treated at length in the books of fiqh.
(لا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلا يَخْرُجْنَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ) لا is prohibitive; تخرجون [sic] is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi; من بيوتهنّ is attached to تخرجوهنّ. As for ولا يخرجن: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is also prohibitive; يخرجن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn in the position of jussive, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil. The two prohibitions were combined only to indicate that even if the husband permitted her to go out, it would not be permissible for her to go out. إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); أن is maṣdariyya, and يأتين is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of accusative by أن; it, together with what falls within its scope, is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of لا يخرجن and of the object of لا تخرجوهنّ, i.e. "they shall not go out, and you shall not put them out, in any state except in the state of their committing a shameful deed". بفاحشة is attached to يأتين, and مبينة is a naʿt (adjective) of فاحشة.
(وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); تلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the things mentioned, and حدود الله is the khabar (predicate). The wāw is a conjunction; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يتعدّ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and حدود الله is the mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ links the apodosis because it is joined with قد; ظلم نفسه is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.
(لا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً) A new (mustaʾnafa) clause set out to give the reason for the content of the condition; more discussion of this shift (iltifāt) will come in the section on rhetoric. لا is negating; تدري is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil is "you". لعلّ and its noun, and the clause يحدث is its khabar; بعد ذلك is an adverb attached to يحدث, and أمرا is the object of يحدث. The clause لعلّ الله etc. stands in place of the two objects of تدري, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing by the [particle of] hope. This has been found problematic, in that the grammarians did not count hope (al-tarajjī) among the suspending elements; so the clause would be new.
(فَإِذا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ فارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition, and the clause بلغن is in the position of genitive by annexation; أجلهنّ is the mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is linking; أمسكوهنّ is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; بمعروف is a ḥāl; أو فارقوهنّ بمعروف is conjoined to what precedes.
(وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ) أشهدوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and ذوي is the mafʿūl bihi; it is the dual of ذا meaning "possessor". منكم is an adjective of ذوي عدل. أقيموا is conjoined to أشهدوا, الشهادة is the mafʿūl bihi, and لله is attached to أقيموا, i.e. for His sake.
(ذلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يوعظ the khabar; به is attached to يوعظ, and من is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause كان is the ṣila (relative clause); the noun of كان is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", and the clause يؤمن is the khabar of كان; بالله is attached to يؤمن, and اليوم الآخر is conjoined to بالله.
(وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is new, brought in as a digression upon the mention of the believers; some have made it parenthetical. من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يتّق is the protasis, jussive by the dropping of the weak letter, and الله is the mafʿūl bihi. يجعل is the apodosis; له is attached to يجعل or is in the position of the second object; مخرجا is the object of يجعل. يرزقه is conjoined to يجعل; من حيث is attached to يرزقه, and the clause لا يحتسب is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb, which is حيث, to it.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ) Conjoined to what precedes. من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يتوكل is the protasis and على الله is attached to يتوكل. The fāʾ is linking; هو is a mubtadaʾ and حسبه the khabar, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً) The clause gives the reason for what precedes. إنّ and its noun, and بالغ is its khabar, with أمره as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). It has also been read بالغٌ with tanwīn and أمرَه in the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of بالغ, because it is an active participle. قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); جعل الله is a verb and its fāʿil; لكل شيء is attached to جعل if it means "create", or is in the position of a fronted second object if it means "make into". أمرا is the mafʿūl bihi in either case [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic word here is قدرا].

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «لا تدري لعلّ الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا» there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the second person. Its benefit is to confront the transgressor directly with the address, out of greater concern to deter from transgression. Some have blundered and thought that the address is to the Prophet. The meaning is: whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself and harmed her [Translator's note: the source prints «وأضربها», evidently for «وأضرّ بها» "and harmed her", i.e. the wife]; so you, O transgressor, do not know the outcome of the matter and what it may lead to: perhaps Allah will bring about in your heart, after that transgression which you ventured upon, something that calls for the opposite of what you did, so that He replaces your hatred of her with love, your aversion to her with turning towards her, and your avoidance with contentment.

dervis-irab:4-7.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاللَّائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); اللائي is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يئسن is the ṣila (relative clause), and من المحيض is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يئسن; من نسائكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial). إن is conditional and ارتبتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʾ is linking; عدّتهنّ is a mubtadaʾ and ثلاثة أشهر its khabar (predicate); the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. It has also been said that the apodosis [i.e. فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر] is the khabar of اللائي, and that the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "then know that it is three months", the conditional clause and its apodosis then being parenthetical. The first is preferable, because of its simplicity and because it dispenses with omission.
(وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ) The wāw is a conjunction; اللائي is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "likewise" or "like them", i.e. their ʿidda is three months. If it were said that it is conjoined to اللائي يئسن as a conjunction of single words, and that the predication about all of them is His saying فعدتهنّ, that would be a good view. The clause لم يحضن is the ṣila. أولات الأحمال is a mubtadaʾ, and you may conjoin it in sequence to what precedes. أجلهنّ is a mubtadaʾ; أن and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) which is the khabar of أجلهنّ; حملهنّ is the object; and the clause is the khabar of أولات. الأحمال is the plural of حَمْل with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, like صحب and أصحاب, which is what is in the belly or on the top of a tree; and الحِمْل with kasra is what is on a back or a head.
(وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْراً) Its i'rab has been given several times, so refresh your memory of it; من أمره is a ḥāl.
(ذلِكَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ أَنْزَلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ وَيُعْظِمْ لَهُ أَجْراً) ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned about the ʿidda and its details; أمر الله is the khabar, and the clause أنزله إليكم is a ḥāl. ومن يتّق الله is a conditional noun and its verb [i.e. the protasis]; يكفّر is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and عن سيئاته is attached to يكفّر [Translator's note: so in the source; what is attached to يكفّر is عنه, while سيئاته is its object]. ويعظم له أجرا is conjoined to the apodosis; له is attached to يعظم and أجرا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُمْ مِنْ وُجْدِكُمْ) The clause explains the fear of Allah stipulated in His saying, the Exalted: «ومن يتق الله». أسكنوهنّ is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi. من حيث is attached to أسكنوهنّ, so من would be for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is the partitive من, whose partitioned [noun] is omitted; its meaning is "lodge them in a place of where you dwell", i.e. part of the place of your dwelling, like His saying, the Exalted, يغضّوا من أبصارهم, i.e. بغضّ أبصارهم [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «بعض أبصارهم» "part of their gaze"]. Qatāda said: if there is only one house, he should lodge her in one of its sides». Al-Rāzī and al-Kisāʾī said: «من is redundant (ṣila), and the meaning is "lodge them where you dwell"», so the adverb would be attached to أسكنوهنّ; but the redundancy of من in an affirmative statement does not accord with the doctrine of the Basrans. The clause سكنتم is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. من وجدكم is a badal (substitute) of the preposition and genitive noun before it, with repetition of the preposition. Al-Zamakhsharī said it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and Abū Ḥayyān objected to him that repetition of the governor is unknown in ʿaṭf bayān. الوُجد with ḍamma on the wāw is capacity and ability. In al-Mukhtār: «وجد في المال wujdan, with ḍamma, fatḥa or kasra on the wāw, and also jidatan with kasra, i.e. he became rich».
(وَلا تُضآرُّوهُنَّ لِتُضَيِّقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ) The wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تضارّوهنّ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi. The lām is for causation; تضيّقوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تضارّوهم [sic]. The object of تضيّقوا is omitted, its implied form being "the dwellings" or "the maintenance"; عليهنّ is attached to تضيّقوا.
(وَإِنْ كُنَّ أُولاتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنْفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّى يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ) The wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; كنّ is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, the nūn is its noun and أولات حمل its khabar. The fāʾ links the apodosis; أنفقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and عليهنّ is attached to أنفقوا. حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; يضعن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of accusative by an أن necessarily implied after حتى, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; حتى and its genitive are attached to أنفقوا.
(فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَأْتَمِرُوا بَيْنَكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and إن is conditional; أرضعن is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; لكم is attached to أرضعن, and the object of أرضعن is omitted, its implied form being "a child of theirs". The fāʾ links the apodosis; آتوهنّ is a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; it is an imperative verb], its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; أجورهنّ is a second mafʿūl bihi. ائتمروا is an imperative verb conjoined to آتوهنّ, i.e. let some of you instruct others; al-iʾtimār means mutual consultation (al-taʾāmur), like al-ishtiwār meaning al-tashāwur. بينكم is an adverb attached to ائتمروا, and بمعروف is also attached to ائتمروا.
(وَإِنْ تَعاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ أُخْرى) The wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; تعاسرتم, i.e. you made things difficult for each other, is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of jussive as the protasis. The fāʾ links the apodosis; the sīn is a particle of futurity; ترضع is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; له is attached to سترضع, and أخرى is the fāʿil. The pronoun in له refers back to the father.
(لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ وَمَنْ قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتاهُ اللَّهُ) The lām is the lām of command; ينفق is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām; ذو سعة is the fāʿil and من سعته is attached to ينفق. The wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussivizing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; قدر, in the passive form, is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, i.e. his provision was straitened for him; عليه is attached to قدر and رزقه is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The fāʾ links the apodosis; the lām is the lām of command and ينفق an imperfect verb jussive by the lām, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. مما is attached to ينفق, and the clause آتاه الله is the ṣila of ما.
(لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِلَّا ما آتاها) The clause is new (mustaʾnafa). لا is negating; يكلف is an imperfect verb, nominative; الله is the fāʿil and نفسا the mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ما is a second mafʿūl bihi and the clause آتاها is the ṣila of ما.
(سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْراً) Also a new statement, set out to confirm the promise to the poor that the doors of provision will be opened. The sīn is a particle of futurity; يجعل is an imperfect verb, nominative, and الله is the fāʿil; بعد عسر is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the second object of يجعل, and يسرا is the first object of يجعل.

dervis-irab:8-12.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّها وَرُسُلِهِ) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement set out to confirm Allah's promise of victory. كأيّن is predicative (khabariyya), meaning كم ("how many"); it has been discussed in detail in Āl ʿImrān. من قرية is the tamyīz (specification) of كأين, and it [كأين] is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause عتت, i.e. turned away, is the khabar (predicate); عن أمر ربها is attached to (mutaʿalliq) عتت, and رسله is conjoined to ربها.
(فَحاسَبْناها حِساباً شَدِيداً وَعَذَّبْناها عَذاباً نُكْراً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; حاسبناها is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حسابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and شديدا a naʿt (adjective). عذبناها is conjoined to حاسبناها; عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and نكرا a naʿt; it is with ḍamma or sukūn on the kāf, these being two readings, meaning hideous and ugly, exceeding the limit.
(فَذاقَتْ وَبالَ أَمْرِها وَكانَ عاقِبَةُ أَمْرِها خُسْراً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ذاقت is a past verb, the tāʾ being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to قرية; وبال أمرها is the mafʿūl bihi. كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, عاقبة أمرها its noun and خسرا its khabar.
(أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) The clause explains what precedes, in emphasis of the threat. أعدّ الله is a past verb and its fāʿil; لهم is attached to أعدّ; عذابا is the mafʿūl bihi and شديدا a naʿt. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you know that, then fear Allah". يا is a vocative particle, and أولي الألباب is a one addressed (munādā) in a genitive construct (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural.
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَدْ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْراً) الذين is a naʿt of the one addressed or a badal (substitute) from it, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause). قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); أنزل الله is a verb and its fāʿil; إليكم is attached to أنزل, and ذكرا is the mafʿūl bihi.
(رَسُولًا يَتْلُوا عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيِّناتٍ) Concerning the accusative of رسولا there are views of almost equal weight, which we set out for you below:
1- It is made accusative by the nunated maṣdar (verbal noun) before it, namely ذكرا, just as [the maṣdar] governs in «أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة يتيما», and as the poet said:
بضرب السيوف رؤوس قوم ... أزلنا هامهنّ عن المقيل
(By the swords' striking the heads of a people, we removed their skulls from their resting place [i.e. the necks].)
Al-Zajjāj and al-Fārisī held this i'rab.
2- It is a badal from ذكرا, [the Messenger] being made the remembrance itself by way of hyperbole; al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this.
3- It is a badal from ذكرا on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf in the first, its implied form being "one possessing a remembrance, a Messenger".
4- It is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, i.e. "He sent a Messenger", because what precedes indicates it.
5- It is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb by way of incitement (al-ighrāʾ), i.e. "follow and hold fast to a Messenger whose description is this".
The clause يتلو عليكم is in the position of accusative as an adjective; عليكم is attached to يتلو, آيات الله is the mafʿūl bihi, and مبينات is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(لِيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ) The lām is for causation; يخرج is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يتلو. الذين is the mafʿūl bihi and what follows is the ṣila; من الظلمات is attached to يخرج, and إلى النور is also attached to يخرج.
(وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and بالله is attached to يؤمن; يعمل is conjoined to يؤمن, and صالحا is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a righteous deed", or a mafʿūl bihi. يدخله is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is a first mafʿūl bihi and جنات a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of جنات. خالدين is a ḥāl of the hāʾ, the meaning of «من» having been observed after its wording was observed; فيها is attached to خالدين, as is the adverb أبدا.
(قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقاً) The clause is a second ḥāl, and here the wording of من has been observed. قد is a particle of realisation; أحسن الله is a verb and its fāʿil; له is attached to أحسن, and رزقا is the mafʿūl bihi.
(اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause خلق is the ṣila; سبع سموات is the object; من الأرض is a ḥāl; مثلهنّ is conjoined to سبع سموات, or accusative by a verb implied after the wāw, i.e. "and He created the like of them from the earth". It has also been read مثلُهنّ in the nominative, as a postponed mubtadaʾ, with the preposition and its genitive noun before it as a fronted khabar.
(يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) The clause is new. يتنزل الأمر is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. the revelation; بينهنّ is attached to يتنزل. The lām is the lām of causation; تعلموا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the lām and its genitive are also attached to يتنزل. أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of تعلموا.
(وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً) The wāw is a conjunction; أنّ and its noun, and the clause قد أحاط is its khabar; بكل شيء is attached to أحاط, and علما is a tamyīz converted from the fāʿil.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها» there is a loose metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is locality (al-maḥalliyya): naming the place and meaning those in it. Many parallels of it have preceded.
2- In His saying «ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور» there are two explicit metaphors (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He likened disbelief to darkness, then omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it was likened to; and He likened faith to light, and likewise omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it was likened to.

farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾. So when a man wants to divorce his wife for the ʿidda (waiting period), he should wait until she has one menstrual period, then divorce her; when she has a menstrual period after the divorce, he divorces her again; and if she has a period after the two divorces, he divorces her a third time. This is divorce for the ʿidda; she is then irrevocably separated from him and is not lawful for him until she marries another husband.
Divorce according to the Sunna is that he divorces her while she is in a state of purity in which there has been no intercourse, then leaves her until she has had three menstrual periods. If he does that, she is separated from him, and marrying her is not lawful for him except with a new dowry, and he has no right to take her back.
His saying: ﴿وَأَحْصُواْ ٱلْعِدَّةَ﴾: [i.e.] the menstrual periods.
His saying: ﴿لاَ تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِن بُيُوتِهِنَّ﴾.
[That is,] those in which they were divorced; and they are not to go out of their own accord ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾. Some said: except that they commit an indecency [— except that she commits an offence liable to a ḥadd punishment, so that she is brought out for it to be carried out on her. And some said: except that they commit an indecency] — except that they disobey and go out, for her going out is a manifest indecency.
His saying: ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾.
He is saying: [keep them] in the remaining divorce on fair terms, or release them on fair terms. He said: and "fair terms" (maʿrūf) means kindness.
His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمْراً﴾.
This is the taking back [of the wife] in the two divorces.
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾.
When she has a period after the two divorces, up until she has the third and has not yet bathed, he may take her back as long as she has not bathed from the third period.

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْراً﴾ ﴿رَّسُولاً﴾.
It came down in the Book with رسول in the accusative, and that is the [proper] Arabic way. Had it been رسولٌ in the nominative, it would be correct, because ذكرا is the end of a verse, and starting afresh (istiʾnāf) after verse-ends is good. Similar to it is His saying: "التائبون", preceded by: ﴿إِنَّ اللهَ اشْتَرَى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; when He said: ﴿وذلك هو الفوزُ العظيمُ﴾, a fresh start was made with the nominative. Similar to it: ﴿وتَرَكَهُمْ فى ظُلُمَاتٍ لا يُبْصِِرُونَ، صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ﴾. And similar to it: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ﴾, then He said: ﴿فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُريدُ﴾, which is an indefinite word describing a definite one, so a fresh start was made with the nominative, because it comes after a verse-end.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾.
[I.e.] He created seven [and created of the earth the like of them]. Had it been read "مثلُهن" [in the nominative], since the verb is not overtly expressed, it would be correct.
You say in speech: رأيت لأخيك إبلا، ولوالدك شاء كثير (I saw camels belonging to your brother, and your father has many sheep), when the verb is not expressed [with the second].
He said: He means that with the latter [noun], the nominative and the accusative are both permissible when the latter has an adjective that takes the nominative; so draw analogies from it, if Allah wills.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ﴾.
The readers all read it with tanwīn [بالغٌ أمرَه]. Had it been read: بالغ أمرِه [in the genitive construct], it would be correct; and had it been read: بالغٌ أمرُه with the nominative, it would be permissible.
[Translator's note: the lemma in the printed text appears in the genitive-construct form, while the comment states that all readers read it with tanwīn.]

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: [200/b] ﴿وَٱللاَّئِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ ٱلْمَحِيضِ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمْ إِنِ ٱرْتَبْتُمْ﴾.
He is saying: if you are in doubt and do not know what her waiting period is. They mention that Muʿādh ibn Jabal asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: We know the waiting period of the woman who menstruates; what is the waiting period of the old woman who has despaired [of menstruation]? Then there came down: ﴿ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاَثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ﴾. A man stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah! What is the waiting period of the young girl who has not menstruated? He said: "And those who have not menstruated" are like the old woman who has despaired: her waiting period is three months. Another stood up and said: And the pregnant women, what is their waiting period? Then there came down: ﴿وَأُوْلاَتُ ٱلأَحْمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾. So when the pregnant woman gives birth to what is in her womb she becomes lawful for husbands, even if her dead husband is still on the bier, not yet buried.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: according to what each of you can afford. If he is well-off, he provides amply for her in housing and maintenance; and if he is in straitened means, then according to that. Then He said: ﴿وَإِن كُنَّ أُوْلاَتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنفِقُواْ عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾: he spends on her from the share of what is in her womb. Then He said: ﴿فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾: the wage for nursing.
His saying: ﴿وَأْتَمِرُواْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾.
He is saying: let the woman not harm her husband, and let him not harm her. The readers have agreed on ḍamma on the واو of "وُجْدكم" and on ḍamma on the قاف of "قُدِر" [and on reading it light]; had they read قُدِّر it would be correct.
And had they read مِنْ "وَجْدِكم" it would be correct, because it is the dialect of Banū Tamīm.

farraa:8-9.t:
His saying: ﴿فَحَاسَبْنَاهَا حِسَاباً شَدِيداً﴾.
In the Hereafter, ﴿وَعَذَّبْنَاهَا عَذَاباً نُّكْراً﴾ in this world; it is [a case of] what is put first and what is put last (muqaddam wa-muʾakhkhar). Then He said: ﴿فَذَاقَتْ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهَا﴾ of the punishment of this world, ﴿وَكَانَ عَاقِبَةُ أَمْرِهَا خُسْراً﴾: the Fire and its punishment.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The conditional clause, the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لعدَّتهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «هنَّ» in «طلِّقوهن». The clause «واتقوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أحصوا»; «ربكم» is a badal (substitute) from the Divine Name; the clause «لا تخرجوهنَّ» is resumptive. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يأتين» is excepted from the generality of states, i.e.: they are not to go out in any state except the state of their committing an indecency; the conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «لا تدري» is resumptive; the clause «لعل الله يحدث» stands in place of the two objects of (درى), «لعل» being among the suspending [particles] (al-muʿalliqāt).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding conditional clause {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «بمعروف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أمسكوهنَّ»; «ذوي» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is dual; the preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «ذوي عدل»; «من» is a relative noun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to the second object of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «حيث» is an adverbial noun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يرزقه», and the clause «يحتسب» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «ومن يتوكل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «من يتق»; the clause «قد جعل» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لكل شيء» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قدرا».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «واللائي يئسن..» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من نسائكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nūn in «يئسن»; the clause «إن ارتبتم فعدَّتهن ثلاثة» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «اللائي», and the clause «فعدَّتهن ثلاثة» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «إن». His words «واللائي لم يحضن»: a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «اللائي يئسن»; his words «وأولات»: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the nominal clause «أجلهن أن يضعن»; the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to the second object of «يجعل»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من أمره» is attached to a ḥāl from «يسرا».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «أنزله» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أمر الله»; the conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «يعظم».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من وجدكم» is a badal (substitute) from «من حيث»; the clause «وإن كن» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أسكنوهن»; «أولات» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause «فإن أرضعن» is conjoined to the clause «إن كن»; the clause «وأتمروا» is conjoined to the clause «فآتوهن»; the preposition and its genitive noun «بمعروف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «وأتمروا»; and the clause «وإن تعاسرتم» is conjoined to the clause «إن أرضعن».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The lām in «لينفق» is the lām of command, governing the jussive; the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ينفق»; the preposition and its genitive noun «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينفق»; the clause «لا يكلف الله» is resumptive; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «ما» is a relative noun, second object; the clause «سيجعل» is resumptive; «بعد» is an adverb attached to the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The wāw is resumptive; «كأين» is a noun alluding to a number (ism kināya), a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «من قرية» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كأين»; the clause «عتت» is the khabar (predicate) of «كأين»; the clause «فحاسبناها» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «عتت»; «حسابا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «فذاقت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {عَذَّبْنَاهَا}, and the clause «وكان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فاتقوا» is resumptive; «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause «قد أنزل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «رسولا» is a badal (substitute); the clause «يتلو» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; «مبينات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آيات الله»; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليخرج» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يتلو»; the conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «قد أحسن» is a ḥāl clause from the hāʾ in «يدخله».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «الله الذي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «من الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مثلهن»; «مثلهن» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «سبع»; the clause «يتنزل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سبع سماوات»; the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «لتعلموا» is attached to «خلق»; the interpreted maṣdar «أن الله على..» stands in place of the two objects of «علم», and the second maṣdar is conjoined to the first; the preposition and its genitive noun «بكل» is attached to «أحاط»; «علما» is tamyīz (specification).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying, Exalted is He, بَالغ أمره: الأمر is accusative by بالغ, because it has a future sense; it has also been read with annexation [بالغُ أمرِه]. Al-Farrāʾ permitted in ordinary speech بالغٌ أمرُه, with tanwīn, with الأمر nominative by بالغ, or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with بالغ its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of إنّ.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying واللائي يئسن: اللائي is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and يئسن with what follows it up to نسائكم is its ṣila (relative clause). وإن ارتبتم is a condition; فعدتهن is a mubtadaʾ, and ثلاثة أشهر its khabar (predicate); the فاء is the apodosis of the condition; and the condition with its apodosis and what is attached to it is a khabar about اللائي. The implied form is "if you are in doubt about them, then the term of their waiting period is three months". The singular of اللائي is التي.
His saying وَأولَات الْأَحْمَال: a mubtadaʾ; أجلهن is a second mubtadaʾ and أن يضعن the khabar — أن is in the position of the nominative, it and the verb being a maṣdar (verbal noun) — and the second [mubtadaʾ] with its khabar is the khabar of the first. It is also possible that أجلهن is a badal (substitute) of أولات, with أن يضعن the khabar, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). The singular of أولات is ذات.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying وَإِن كن أولات حمل: in كان is its noun and أولات is the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "if the divorced women are pregnant, then spend on them".

mekki-muskil:10-11.t:
His saying قد أنزل الله إِلَيْكُم ذكرا رَسُولا: ذكر is accusative by أنزل, and رسول is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ذكر, its implied form being "a reminder possessing a messenger" (ذكرا ذا رسول); then the muḍāf was omitted. It is also said that رسول is accusative as a badal (substitute) of ذكر, with رسول meaning a message (رسالة). It is also said that it is a badal and رسول is in its basic sense, but the meaning is "Allah has made manifest a reminder, a messenger", because أنزل indicates making manifest a matter that did not exist; so on this meaning it does not mean "a message". In both cases it is the badal of a thing for a thing that is identical to it.
It is also said that it is accusative by an implied أرسلنا ("We sent"); it is also said that it is accusative by an implied أعني ("I mean"); it is also said that it is accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "follow a messenger" or "hold to a messenger"; it is also said that it is accusative by a verb that ذكرا indicates, its implied form being "Allah has sent down to you a reminder: remember a messenger" (تذكروا رسولا), or "so remember a messenger" (فذكر رسولا). It is also said that it is accusative by ذكر, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that governs as a verb does; its implied form is "Allah has sent down to you that you should remember a messenger".
His saying يتلو: a naʿt of رسول.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying لِتَعْلَمُوا: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تنزل; it is also said: to خلق.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا أيها النبي﴾: «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); «ها» is for drawing attention; and «النبي» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.
﴿إذا﴾: «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition.
﴿طلقتم النساء﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿طلقتم النساء﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the adverb's annexation to it.
﴿فطلقوهن﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb), and «طلقوهن» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi.
﴿لعدتهن﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «عدتهن» is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «طلقوهن», on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: «لأول عدتهن» (at the beginning of their waiting period).
﴿وأحصوا العدة واتقوا الله ربكم﴾: «أحصوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to the imperative before it; «العدة» is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause «واتقوا» is conjoined to the clause «أحصوا»; and «ربكم» is a badal (substitute) from the Name of Majesty.
﴿لا تخرجوهن من بيوتهن ولا يخرجن إلا أن يأتين بفاحشة مبينة﴾: «لا» is prohibitive; «تخرجوهن» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لا»; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; «من بيوتهن» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تخرجوهن». «ولا يخرجن»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is likewise prohibitive. «يخرجن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of a jussive, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «أن» is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); «يأتين» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of an accusative by «أن», and it, together with what falls within its scope, is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; «بفاحشة» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يأتين﴾; and «مبينة» is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿فاحشة﴾.
﴿وتلك حدود الله ومن يتعد حدود الله فقد ظلم نفسه﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «حدود الله» is the khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. The wāw is a conjunction; «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «يتعد» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its being jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; «حدود الله» is a mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is joined with «قد»; «ظلم نفسه» is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».
﴿لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position. «لا» is negating; «تدري» is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil is «أنت» (you); «لعل» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) conveying hope (tarajjī); the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause «يحدث» is its khabar; «بعد ذلك» is an adverb attached to «يحدث»; «أمرًا» is the object of «يحدث»; and the clause «لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرًا» stands in place of the two objects of «تدري», which is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing by the [particle of] hope.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فإذا بلغن أجلهن فأمسكوهن بمعروف أو فارقوهن بمعروف﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إذا» is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause «بلغن» is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; «أجلهن» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is linking; «أمسكوهن» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi; «بمعروف» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and «أو فارقوهن بمعروف» is conjoined to what precedes.
﴿وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله﴾: «أشهدوا» is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; «ذوي» is a mafʿūl bihi, and it is the dual of «ذا» in the sense of «صاحب» (possessor of); «منكم» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «ذوي عدل»; «أقيموا» is conjoined to «أشهدوا»; «الشهادة» is a mafʿūl bihi; and «لله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقيموا﴾, i.e. for His sake.
﴿ذلكم يوعظ به من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر﴾: «ذلكم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يوعظ» is the khabar (predicate); «به» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يوعظ﴾; «مَن» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause «كان» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The noun of «كان» is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هو» (he); the clause «يؤمن» is the khabar of «كان»; «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤمن﴾; and «اليوم الآخر» is conjoined to «بالله».
﴿ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا﴾: the wāw is for resumption (istiʾnāf), and the clause is resumptive or parenthetical; on either view it has no grammatical position. «مَن» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «يتق» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), made jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter; the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi; «يجعل» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يجعل», or in the place of the second object; and «مخرجًا» is the object of «يجعل».

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب﴾: «يرزقه» is conjoined to «يجعل»; «من حيث» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يرزقه﴾; and the clause ﴿لا يحتسب﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb, namely «حيث», to it.
﴿ومن يتوكل على الله فهو حسبه﴾: conjoined to what precedes. «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «يتوكل» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «على الله»: «على» is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يتوكل﴾; the fāʾ is linking; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «حسبه» is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».
﴿إن الله بالغ أمره قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا﴾: the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) for what precedes. «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun, «بالغ» is its khabar, and «أمره» is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «جعل الله» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «لكل شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «جعل» if it is in the sense of creating, or in the place of the fronted second object if it is in the sense of making-into (taṣyīr); and «قدرًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿واللائي يئسن من المحيض من نسائكم﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). «اللائي» is a relative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause ﴿يئسن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «من المحيض» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يئسن﴾. «من نسائكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إن ارتبتم فعدتهن ثلاثة أشهر﴾: «إن» is conditional. «ارتبتم» is a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʾ is linking; «عدتهن» is a mubtadaʾ, «ثلاثة» is its khabar (predicate), and «أشهر» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿فعدتهن...﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the condition with its apodosis is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿اللائي﴾. It has also been said: the clause ﴿فعدتهن...﴾ is the khabar of «اللائي», and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: ﴿فاعلموا أنها ثلاثة أشهر﴾ (then know that it is three months); the conditional clause with its apodosis is then parenthetical, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿واللائي يئسن...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿واللائي لم يحضن وأولات الأحمال أجلهن أن يضعن حملهن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «اللائي» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: «فكذلك» (then likewise), or «مثلهن» (like them), i.e.: their waiting period is three months. Had it been said that it is conjoined to «اللائي يئسن» as a conjunction of single words, with «عدتهن» serving as the predicate of them all, that would have been a good view. The clause ﴿لم يحضن﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «أولات الأحمال» is a mubtadaʾ, or else it is coordinated with what precedes; «أجلهن» is a mubtadaʾ; «أن» together with what falls within its scope is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) which is the khabar of «أجلهن»; «حملهن» is an object; and the clause is the khabar of «أولات».
﴿ومن يتق الله يجعل له من أمره يسرا﴾: the wāw is for resumption (istiʾnāf); «مَن» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «يتق» is the protasis, made jussive by the dropping of the weak letter; the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «يجعل» is the apodosis; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يجعل﴾; «من أمره» is a ḥāl; «يسرًا» is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ﴿ومن يتق الله...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ذلك أمر الله أنزله إليكم﴾: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «أمر الله» is the khabar (predicate), and the clause «أنزله إليكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ومن يتق الله يكفر عنه سيئاته ويعظم له أجرا﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); «مَن» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «يتق» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), made jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter; the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «يكفر» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «عن سيئاته» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكفر﴾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic text reads «عنه سيئاته», and «سيئاته» is the object of «يكفر».]»; «يعظم له أجرًا» is conjoined to the apodosis; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعظم﴾; «أجرًا» is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ﴿ومن يتق الله...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
