﴿أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم﴾: «أسكنوهن» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «من حيث» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أسكنوهن﴾, so «من» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); it has also been said that it is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya), and it has also been said that it is redundant (ṣila), i.e.: «أسكنوهن حيث سكنتم» (lodge them where you dwell), the adverb being attached to ﴿أسكنوهن﴾. The clause ﴿سكنتم﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it. ﴿من وجدكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted badal (substitute) from the preposition and genitive noun before it, with the repetition of the preposition; it has also been said: an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The clause ﴿أسكنوهن﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is prohibitive; «تضاروهن» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لا», the sign of its being jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. The lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); «تضيقوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām of reason, the sign of its being accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. The interpreted maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb is made genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تضاروهن﴾. The object of «تضيقوا» is omitted, its implied form being «المساكن» (the dwellings) or «النفقة» (the maintenance); and ﴿عليهن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تضيقوا﴾.
﴿وإن كن أولات حمل فأنفقوا عليهن حتى يضعن حملهن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «كن» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nūn is its noun, and «أولات حمل» is its khabar (predicate). The fāʾ links the apodosis; «أنفقوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿عليهن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنفقوا﴾; «حتى» is a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; «يضعن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of an accusative by «أن» necessarily implied after «حتى», and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; «حتى» together with what it puts in the genitive is attached to ﴿أنفقوا﴾.
﴿فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن وأتمروا بينكم بمعروف﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «أرضعن» is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرضعن﴾; the object of «أرضعن» is omitted, its implied form being: «ولدًا منهن» (a child of theirs). The fāʾ links the apodosis; «آتوهن» is a past verb «[Translator's note: so in the source; «آتوهن» is an imperative verb.]», its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «أجورهن» is a second mafʿūl bihi. «ائتمروا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «آتوهن», i.e. let some of you instruct others; «بينكم» is an adverb attached to ﴿ائتمروا﴾, and «بمعروف» is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿ائتمروا﴾.
﴿وإن تعاسرتم فسترضع له أخرى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «تعاسرتم» is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ links the apodosis; the sīn is a particle of the future; «ترضع» is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «سترضع»; «أخرى» is the fāʿil; and the pronoun in «له» refers back to the father.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿لينفق ذو سعة من سعته ومن قدر عليه رزقه فلينفق مما آتاه الله﴾: the lām is the lām of command; «ينفق» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by the lām; «ذو سعة» is the fāʿil (agent); «من سعته» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينفق﴾. The wāw is a conjunction; «من» is a conditional noun that makes [the verb] jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «قدر», built for the one whose agent is not named (passive), is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), i.e. his provision is restricted for him; «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدر﴾; «رزقه» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The fāʾ links the apodosis; the lām is the lām of command; «ينفق» is an imperfect verb made jussive by the lām, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of «من». «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينفق﴾, and the clause «آتاه الله» is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «لا» is negating; «يكلف» is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); «الله» is the fāʿil; «نفسًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «ما» is a second mafʿūl bihi; and the clause ﴿آتاها﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿سيجعل الله بعد عسر يسرا﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. The sīn is a particle of the future; «يجعل» is an imperfect verb in the nominative; «الله» is the fāʿil; «بعد عسر» is an adverb attached to an omitted [word], which is the second object of «يجعل»; and «يسرًا» is the first object of «يجعل».

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وكأين من قرية عتت عن أمر ربها ورسله﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. «كأين» is declarative (khabariyya), in the sense of «كم» (how many); «من قرية» is the tamyīz (specification) of «كأين», and it is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «عتت» is the khabar (predicate); «عن أمر ربها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عتت﴾; and «رسله» is conjoined to «ربها».
﴿فحاسبناها حسابا شديدا وعذبناها عذابا نكرا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «حاسبناها» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «حسابًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «شديدًا» is a naʿt (adjective); «عذبناها» is conjoined to «حاسبناها»; «عذابًا» stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); and «نكرًا» is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فذاقت وبال أمرها وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ذاقت» is a past verb, the tāʾ being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to «قرية»; «وبال أمرها» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, «عاقبة أمرها» is its noun, and «خسرًا» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿أعد الله لهم عذابا شديدا﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or it is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the clause ﴿وكان عاقبة أمرها خسرًا﴾, or a badal of part from whole. «أعد الله» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعد﴾; «عذابًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «شديدًا» is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿فاتقوا الله يا أولي الألباب﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. if you have come to know that, then fear Allah. «يا» is a vocative particle, and «أولي الألباب» is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, made accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural.
﴿الذين آمنوا قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا﴾: «الذين» is a naʿt of the one addressed, or a badal from it; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «أنزل الله» is a verb and its fāʿil; «إليكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنزل﴾; and «ذكرًا» is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿رسولا يتلو عليكم آيات الله مبينات﴾: «رسولًا» is made accusative (manṣūb) by the nunated maṣdar (verbal noun) before it, namely «ذكرًا»; or: it is a badal (substitute) from ﴿ذكرًا﴾, [the Messenger being made] the very remembrance by way of hyperbole; it has also been said: a badal from ﴿ذكرًا﴾ on the assumption of a muḍāf omitted from the first, its implied form being: «ذا ذكر رسولًا» (one possessing remembrance, a Messenger); it has also been said: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. «أرسل رسولًا» (He sent a Messenger); and it has also been said: the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e.: «اتبعوا» (follow). The clause «يتلوا عليكم» «[Translator's note: so spelled in the source, for «يتلو».]» is in the position of an accusative as an adjective (ṣifa); «عليكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتلو﴾; «آيات الله» is a mafʿūl bihi; and «مبينات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ليخرج الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من الظلمات إلى النور﴾: the lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); «يخرج» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb is made genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يتلو﴾. «الذين» is a mafʿūl bihi, and «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «من الظلمات» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخرج﴾, and «إلى النور» is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿يخرج﴾.
﴿ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); «من» is a conditional noun that makes [the verb] jussive, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject); «يؤمن» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «بالله»: the bāʾ is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يؤمن﴾; «يعمل» is conjoined to «يؤمن»; «صالحًا» is a mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يعمل﴾, or it stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e.: «عمل عملًا صالحًا» (does a righteous deed); «يدخله» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the hāʾ being the first mafʿūl bihi, and «جنات» is the second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «جنات»; the clause ﴿ومن يؤمن بالله...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «خالدين» is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, the meaning of ﴿من﴾ being taken into account after its wording had been taken into account; «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدين﴾, and so is the adverb «أبدًا».
﴿قد أحسن الله له رزقا﴾: the clause is a second ḥāl, and here the wording of «من» has been taken into account. «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «أحسن الله» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحسن﴾; and «رزقًا» is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿الله الذي خلق سبع سماوات ومن الأرض مثلهن﴾: «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الذي» is its khabar (predicate); the clause «خلق» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «سبع سماوات» is an object; «من الأرض» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مثلهن»; and «مثلهن» is conjoined to «سبع سماوات», or it is made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) verb after the wāw, i.e.: «وخلق مثلهن من الأرض» (and He created the like of them of the earth).
﴿يتنزل الأمر بينهن لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «يتنزل الأمر» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «بينهن» is a preposition and its genitive noun «[Translator's note: so in the source; «بين» is an adverb.]», attached to ﴿يتنزل﴾. The lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl); «تعلموا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb is made genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to ﴿يتنزل﴾. «إن» «[Translator's note: so in the source, for «أنّ».]» together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ﴿تعلموا﴾.
﴿وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause «قد أحاط» is its khabar; «بكل شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحاط﴾; and «علمًا» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the fāʿil.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ: a naʿt (adjective) of «أيّ». If you pronounce it with hamza, it is derived from «أنبأ», i.e. "to inform". If you do not pronounce the hamza, it may be from «أنبأ» with the hamza lightened, and there is a subtle point of Arabic in this: when the hamza is lightened and a quiescent letter precedes it, the rule is that its vowel is thrown onto what precedes it, but that is not permissible here. The reason for this is that this yāʾ is never vowelled in any circumstances, so since it could not be vowelled, «نبيّ» and «خطيّة» were said; if it were according to analogy, «خطيّة» would be said [Translator's note: the text repeats «خطيّة»; presumably a different form was intended]. If you derive it from «نبا ينبو», it has no hamza and the final yāʾ is converted from a wāw. إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ: that is, when you intend that; and this is figurative (majāz). As for the discussion of إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ when before it is يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ, we have mentioned several views about it. It has also been said: it is addressing the Prophet ﷺ with the plural form out of reverence for him, just as one says to an eminent man "you (pl.) did". The meaning is: when you divorce the women with whom you have consummated marriage. فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made this clear on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ: that it is divorce in a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her. وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ: al-Suddī said: that is, keep count of it. وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ: that is, do not go beyond what He has commanded you. لا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلا يَخْرُجْنَ: then He made an exception: إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative. The scholars disagreed about what this indecency (fāḥisha) is. Among the most comprehensive things said about it is that it is disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; this includes every view, because if she commits fornication or steals and is taken out to have the ḥadd punishment carried out, that is included in this, and likewise if she is foul-mouthed or rebellious. وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ: that is, the things He has defined regarding divorce, the waiting period, and that the wife is not to go out. وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ: the alif was dropped for the jussive. فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ: it has been said: that is, he has deprived it of what had been permitted to him, because if he divorces her three times, in whatever circumstance, it is not lawful for him to take her back until she marries another husband; so he has wronged himself by this act. لا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً: most of the exegetes hold that the meaning is that if he divorces her once it is better for him: لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً, namely love for her.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
فَإِذا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ: that is, when they are close to that. فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: that is, with what is due to them from you of maintenance, refraining from foul speech and so on. أَوْ فارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: by handing over their dowries to them and what is due to them. وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ: most of the exegetes hold that this concerns taking back (al-rajʿa). From Ibn ʿAbbās: he should take witnesses to the divorce and the taking back, except that if he does not take witnesses, nothing is held against him. وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ: that is, bear witness to the truth when you testify and when you deliver testimony, as al-Suddī said: that is, in the truth.
ذلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ: «ذلكم» addresses a plurality and speaks of a single thing, because the end of the word is for the one you address, and its beginning is for what you speak of or ask about. وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً: the exegetes hold that the meaning is that if he fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and divorces once, he has a way out: if he wishes to remarry [her], he remarries; but if he does not fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and divorces three times, he has no way out. This view is soundly reported from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn ʿAbbās with chains of transmission that cannot be rejected. Ibn ʿUlayya reported from Ayyūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr, from Mujāhid, who said: I was with Ibn ʿAbbās when a man came to him and said: "O Ibn ʿAbbās, I have divorced my wife three times." Ibn ʿAbbās lowered his head for a long while, then raised his head to the man and said:
"One of you commits a piece of folly and then says: 'O Ibn ʿAbbās!' You divorced three times, so she has become unlawful to you until she marries a husband other than you, and Allah has not made a way out for you; had you feared Him, He would have made a way out for you (pl.)." Then he recited: وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً. And the saying of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, whose authenticity cannot be rejected, is that he said, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning [the declaration] "unlawful" (al-ḥarām): it counts as three; she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ: Qatāda said: from where he does not hope or expect. وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ: that is, his sufficiency; «أحسبني الشيءُ» means "the thing sufficed me". This is the end of the statement; then He said: إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ. Masrūq said: that is, He accomplishes His purpose whether one relies on Him or not, i.e. His decree is carried out. Hārūn the reciter said: in [the reading of] ʿIṣma it is read إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ [i.e. «بالغٌ أمرَه»] [Translator's note: the variant reading is not visible in the vowelled text, which reproduces the standard reading]; and this [the standard reading] is with the tanwīn dropped for lightness. Al-Farrāʾ permitted إِنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أَمْرِهِ [i.e. «بالغٌ أمرُه»] with the nominative [of «أمر»] as the agent of «بالغ»; it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of «إنّ». قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً: that is, [He has set] for divorce and the waiting period a limit at which they end.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: اللَّائِي is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). So whoever makes «إن ارتبتم» attached to His saying لا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ, for him the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ. And whoever takes the construction according to what is reported — that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: "O Messenger of Allah, the young and the old who have despaired of menstruation, and وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ, their waiting period has not been mentioned in the Qur'an", whereupon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: وَاللَّائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ (the verse) — says: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is «إن ارتبتم» and what follows it, and the meaning is: if you do not know and are in doubt about their waiting period, their ruling is this. As for the view of ʿIkrima on the meaning of «إن ارتبتم», that it is "if you are in doubt about the blood and do not know whether it is menstrual blood or irregular bleeding (istiḥāḍa)", فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ — this has been refuted from more than one angle. That is because if the doubt were about the blood, it would have been said «إن ارتبتنّ» (if you women are in doubt), because doubt about blood belongs to the women. Also, despair (al-yaʾs) in Arabic is the cutting off of hope, while doubt (al-irtiyāb) is the existence of hope, so it is impossible for them to coexist. وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ: conjoined to the first; the statement is complete. Then He said: وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ. Abū Jaʿfar said: there are two views about this. One of them is that it applies to every pregnant woman, whether divorced after consummation or widowed: when she gives birth, she becomes lawful [to marry]; this is the view of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb [and] Ibn Masʿūd [Translator's note: the text reads «أبيّ بن كعب بن مسعود»; a "wa-" (and) seems to have dropped out]. The second view is that this applies to divorced women only, and that the widow, if she gives birth before the end of four months and ten days, does not become lawful until four months and ten days have passed; likewise, if four months have passed and she has not given birth, she does not become lawful until she gives birth. This is the view of ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. The first view is more appropriate to the apparent sense of the words, because He, Mighty and Majestic, said وَأُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ in general terms, and no specification occurs except by authoritative instruction (tawqīf) from the Messenger ﷺ. أُولاتُ الْأَحْمالِ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ. أَجَلُهُنَّ: a second mubtadaʾ. أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ: the khabar of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. «أجلهنّ» may also be a badal (substitute) from «أولاتُ», with the khabar being «أن يضعن حملهنّ». وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْراً: the exegetes hold that the meaning is: whoever fears Allah when he wants to divorce, and divorces once as was defined for him, يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْراً, in that remarrying [her] is lawful for him — unlike someone who divorced three times.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: ذلِكَ: that is, that which has been mentioned regarding divorce, menstruation and the waiting periods. أَمْرُ اللَّهِ أَنْزَلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ: so that you follow it. وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ: that is, fears Him by performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden. يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ: that is, He erases his sins. وَيُعْظِمْ لَهُ أَجْراً: that is, He makes his reward abundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: we know of no one who read it other than this way, contrary to the expression «أعظم الله أجرك» (may Allah make your reward great).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ: it has been said that this pronoun refers back to the women in general with whom marriage has been consummated; and it has been said: to women divorced fewer than three times, and that women divorced three times have neither lodging nor maintenance. On that, the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ is sound: al-Awzāʿī reported it from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Abū Salama, from Fāṭima bint Qays, from the Prophet ﷺ. This is also inferred from His saying: وَإِنْ كُنَّ أُولاتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنْفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّى يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ, for He singled out the pregnant women alone; and also, when they are divorced three times they are strangers [to him]. فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ: a condition and its apodosis (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh). وَأْتَمِرُوا بَيْنَكُمْ بِمَعْرُوفٍ: Sufyān said: that is, let some of you urge others. وَإِنْ تَعاسَرْتُمْ: al-Suddī said: that is, if the divorced woman says "I will not nurse him", she is not compelled. The Exalted said: فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ أُخْرى.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ: the lām of command comes with kasra in its basic form, and is made quiescent in فَلْيُنْفِقْ because it is joined to the fāʾ; kasra is also permissible there. Al-Farrāʾ permitted «ومن قُدِرَ عليه رزقُه فلينفقِ مما آتاه الله» [with kasra on the lām], i.e. according to the measure of the straitened provision Allah has given him. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās [on] فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمَّا آتاهُ اللَّهُ: if he has household goods he can sell, he sells them and spends [the proceeds]. لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِلَّا ما آتاها: al-Suddī said: Allah does not burden the poor man with the maintenance of the rich. Ibn Zayd said: He does not burden the poor man with paying zakat and giving alms. سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْراً: that is, either in this world or in the Hereafter, so that the believers may be encouraged to do good.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: «أيّ» is in the genitive by the kāf, and «كأيّن» has come to mean «كم» (how many) for multitude. The meaning is: "and how many people of a town were insolent towards the command of their Lord"; then the muḍāf ilayhi was set in place of the muḍāf. Ibn Zayd said: «عتوا» here means they disobeyed and disbelieved. «العتوّ» in the language is going too far in opposition and disobedience. ʿAmr ibn Abī Salama reported from ʿUmar ibn Sulaymān regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّها (the verse): he said: these are a people who were punished concerning divorce. فَحاسَبْناها: that is, regarding the favours and gratitude. حِساباً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). شَدِيداً: its naʿt (adjective). Ibn Zayd said: the severe reckoning is that in which there is no pardon at all. وَعَذَّبْناها عَذاباً نُكْراً: that is, not usual. Al-Farrāʾ said: it involves putting first and putting later (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), i.e. "We punished it with a terrible punishment in this world, and We will reckon with it a severe reckoning in the Hereafter".

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: فَذاقَتْ وَبالَ أَمْرِها: al-Suddī said: that is, the punishment of its conduct; and its conduct was disbelief and disobedience. وَكانَ عاقِبَةُ أَمْرِها خُسْراً: that is, loss, because they sold the bliss of the Hereafter for a paltry share of this world by following their desires.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً: and that is the punishment of the Fire. فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ: a vocative of a muḍāf. والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «أولي الألباب». قَدْ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْراً: al-Suddī said: the reminder (al-dhikr) is the Qur'an, and the messenger is Muḥammad ﷺ. The implied construction in Arabic on this view is "a reminder possessing a messenger", then [the muḍāf] was omitted, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. It is also possible that «رسول» has the meaning of «رسالة» (message), like أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ
[Maryam: 19], so that «رسولا» would be a badal (substitute) from «ذكر». It is also possible that the implied construction is "We sent a messenger", what preceded in the speech indicating the implied [verb]. Outside the Qur'an, «رسولٌ» in the nominative would be permissible, because «ذكرا» is the end of a verse, and a fresh start after the like of this is better, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي ظُلُماتٍ لا يُبْصِرُونَ صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ [al-Baqara: 17, 18], and likewise إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ [al-Tawba: 11] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse is al-Tawba: 111]; then when the verse was complete He, Mighty and Majestic, said: التَّائِبُونَ الْعابِدُونَ [al-Tawba: 111, 112]; and likewise ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ [al-Burūj: 16] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verses are al-Burūj: 15–16].

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
يَتْلُوا عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيِّناتٍ: a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول». لِيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ: that is, from disbelief to faith. وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ: jussive by the condition. وَيَعْمَلْ: conjoined to it; it may be nominative as being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). صالِحاً: that is, in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: the apodosis (mujāzāh). خالِدِينَ فِيها: as a ḥāl. أَبَداً: an adverb of time. قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقاً: that is, He has made ample for him his food and drink.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ: the name of Allah the Exalted may be a badal (substitute), or [nominative] by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), with «الذي» a naʿt (adjective); it may also be that «اللهُ [الذي] خلق سبع سماوات» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate). وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ: conjoined. Abū Ḥātim reported that ʿĀṣim read وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ [i.e. «مثلُهنّ»], cutting it off from the first and putting it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described.] يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ: it has been said that the pronoun refers back to the heavens. Most commonly in the speech of the Arabs, what is with the hāʾ and nūn (-hunna) is for a small number; so on this basis the pronoun refers back to the heavens. According to the view of Mujāhid, it refers back to the heavens and the earth. لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: the lām of purpose (lām kay) may be attached to «يتنزّل», or it may be attached to «خلق», i.e. He created the heavens and the earth so that you might know the full extent of His power and authority, and that nothing He wants is impossible for Him and nothing He wills resists Him. وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً: that is, and so that you may know, along with your knowledge of His power, that He knows everything His creatures do; so beware, you who oppose His command, of His assault, because of His power over you and because He knows what you do. Making the name explicit was permissible: He did not say «وأنه» (and that He) but said «وأنّ اللهَ», which is more majestic. On this basis the poet's saying is interpreted: [al-Khafīf] 495-
لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغّص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
(I see that nothing outruns death; death has spoiled [life] for the rich and the poor alike.)

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) a vocative, a specified indefinite noun (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative. (النبي) a badal (substitute) for (أيّ) – or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) – following it in the nominative in form. (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لعدتهنّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in (طلقوهنّ), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: "facing the beginning of their ʿidda". (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (ربّكم) an adjective of the name of Majesty (Allah), accusative. (لا) prohibitive and jussive-governing. (من بيوتهنّ) attached to (تخرجوهنّ). (لا) like the first. (يخرجن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of jussive. (إلّا) for exception. (يأتين) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of accusative. (بفاحشة) attached to (يأتين).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتين..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to a ḥāl, i.e. "except as sinners by their committing the indecency" [Note: This ḥāl is an exception from the totality of states, i.e. "let them not go out in any state whatsoever except in the state of their being sinners ..."].
(الواو) resumptive; the demonstrative in (تلك) refers to the preceding rulings. (الواو) conjunction. (من) a conditional noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject). (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (قد) a particle of certainty. (لا) negative; the fāʿil (agent) of (تدري) is a pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you), and the address is to the one who divorces. (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يحدث).
Clause: «النداء ... » (the vocative) has no grammatical position; it is an initial clause.
And the clause: «الشرط وفعله وجوابه ... » (the condition, its verb and its apodosis) has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative [Note: There are many opinions about the vocative addressed to the Prophet; see the tafsīr works for them. It is also permissible for the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis to be in the position of accusative as the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied "say", i.e. "O Prophet, say to your community ..."].
And the clause: «طلّقتم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «طلّقوهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive-governing condition.
And the clause: «أحصوا العدّة» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
And the clause: «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
And the clause: «لا تخرجوهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istinʾāf bayānī).
And the clause: «لا يخرجن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «يأتين ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «تلك حدود ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «من يتعدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «تلك حدود».
And the clause: «يتعدّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together].
And the clause: «قد ظلم نفسه ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «لا تدري ... » has no grammatical position; it is a causal clause.
And the clause: «لعلّ اللَّه يحدث ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: The object of تدري is implied. As for the one who takes (لعل) as suspending the verb, the clause is in the position of accusative, standing in the place of the two objects of تدري].
And the clause: «يحدث ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of لعلّ.
2- (الفاء) resumptive, and the second links to the apodosis. (بمعروف) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of أمسكوهنّ, and the second is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of فارقوهنّ. (منكم) attached to a ḥāl from (ذوي) – or to an adjective of it. (للَّه) attached to (أقيموا) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for the sake of Allah". The demonstrative in (ذلكم) refers to what has been mentioned, from the beginning of the sūra up to here, of rulings. (به) attached to (يوعظ). (من) a relative in the position of nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (باللَّه) attached to (يؤمن). (الواو) resumptive. (من يتّق اللَّه) like «من يتعدّ حدود». (له) attached to an omitted second object (mafʿūl bihi).
And the clause: «بلغن ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «أمسكوهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive-governing condition.
And the clause: «فارقوهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أمسكوهنّ.
And the clause: «أشهدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أمسكوهن.
And the clause: «أقيموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أمسكوهن.
And the clause: «ذلكم يوعظ به ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يوعظ به من كان ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلكم).
And the clause: «كان يؤمن باللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من); and the clause: «يؤمن باللَّه ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كان.
And the clause: «من يتّق ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يتّق ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) (1).
And the clause: «يجعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
3- (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (حيث) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (يرزقه). (لا) negative. (على اللَّه) attached to (يتوكّل). (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (قد) a particle of certainty. (لكلّ) attached to an omitted second object [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from (قدرا), if جعل is taken to include the meaning of "create"].
And the clause: «يرزقه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يجعل ...
And the clause: «لا يحتسب ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «من يتوكّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من يتّق اللَّه ...
And the clause: «يتوكّل على اللَّه ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) (3).
And the clause: «هو حسبه ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «إنّ اللَّه بالغ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «جعل اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is a causal clause.

* Morphology:
(1) يتعدّ: it contains an iʿlāl by deletion, to suit the jussive; its wazn is يتفعّ.
(2) مخرجا: a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun with initial mīm) from the triliteral خرج; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it may also be a noun of place.

* Benefits:
Iltifāt (grammatical shift of person): in the saying of the Exalted لا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ أَمْراً.
A shift from the third person to the second in the saying of the Exalted: لا تَدْرِي. The address in «لا تدري» is to the transgressor, by way of iltifāt, for greater emphasis on deterring from transgression, and not to the Prophet ﷺ as has been said. The meaning is: whoever transgresses the limits of Allah the Exalted has exposed himself to harm, for you do not know, O transgressor, the outcome of the matter.

safi-cedvel:4-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من المحيض) attached to (يئسن). (من نسائكم) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يئسن. (ارتبتم) a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (الواو) conjunction. (اللائي) a relative in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first relative [Note: It is permissible that the relative be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by the first khabar; the conjunction is then a conjunction of clauses]. (يحضن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of jussive. (أجلهنّ) a second mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أن) a maṣdar particle governing the accusative. (يضعن) in the position of accusative by أن. (الواو) resumptive. (من يتّق اللَّه يجعل له) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (2) of this sūra]. (من أمره) attached to a ḥāl from (يسرا), which is the first object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضعن..) is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, i.e.: their term is the delivery of their burden.
Clause: «اللائي يئسن ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يئسن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (اللائي).
And the clause: «إن ارتبتم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللائي); and the clause: «عدّتهنّ ثلاثة أشهر ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «لم يحضن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (اللائي).
And the clause: «أولات الأحمال ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause; and the clause: «أجلهن أن يضعن ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولات ...
And the clause: «يضعن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «من يتّق اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يتق اللَّه ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together].
And the clause: «يجعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
5- The demonstrative in (ذلك) refers to the preceding rulings. (إليكم) attached to (أنزله). (الواو) conjunction. (من يتق اللَّه يكفّر) the i'rab of its like has already been given [Note: in verse (2) of this sūra]. (عنه) attached to (يكفّر), by its inclusion of the meaning "sends down". (يعظم) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (يكفّر) by the wāw. (له) attached to (يعظم).
And the clause: «ذلك أمر اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أنزله إليكم ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from أمر اللَّه, the operator in it being the demonstrative.
And the clause: «من يتّق اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ذلك أمر اللَّه.
And the clause: «يتّق اللَّه ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis].
And the clause: «يكفّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «يعظم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يكفّر.
6- (حيث) an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (أسكنوهنّ) [Note: (من) is partitive – or for the beginning of the range]. (من وجدكم) a badal from حيث with repetition of the preposition. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive and jussive-governing. (اللام) the lām of reason. (تضيّقوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (عليهنّ) attached to (تضيّقوا).. The interpreted maṣdar (أن تضيّقوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (تضارّوهنّ).
(الواو) conjunction. (كنّ) a defective past verb (kāna) in the position of jussive, the protasis. (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (عليهنّ) the second, attached to (أنفقوا). (حتّى) a particle of limit and of genitive. (يضعن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of accusative by an implied أن after حتّى..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضعن) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (أنفقوا).
(الفاء) conjunction. (أرضعن) a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis. (لكم) attached to (أرضعن); the object of the suckling is omitted, i.e. "your children". (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (أجورهنّ) a second object, accusative. (بينكم) an adverb, accusative, attached to (ائتمروا). (بمعروف) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of ائتمروا. (إن تعاسرتم) like إن أرضعن. (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (السين) a particle of futurity. (له) attached to (سترضع)..
And the clause: «أسكنوهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «سكنتم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «لا تضارّوهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أسكنوهنّ.
And the clause: «تضيّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «إن كنّ أولات ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أسكنوهنّ [Note: or it is resumptive].
And the clause: «أنفقوا ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «يضعن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «إن أرضعن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إن كنّ..
And the clause: «آتوهنّ ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «ائتمروا ... » is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause آتوهنّ.
And the clause: «إن تعاسرتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إن أرضعن ...
And the clause: «سترضع له أخرى» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
7- (اللام) the lām of command. (من سعته) attached to (ينفق). (الواو) conjunction. (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (عليه) attached to (قدر). (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (اللام) the lām of command. (ممّا) attached to (ينفق). (لا) negative. (إلّا) for restriction. (ما) a relative in the position of accusative, a second object, the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) being omitted, i.e. "ātāhu iyyāh". (بعد) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted second object.
And the clause: «ينفق ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «من قدر عليه رزقه» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ينفق.
And the clause: «قدر عليه رزقه ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis].
And the clause: «ينفق ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «آتاه اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «لا يكلّف اللَّه نفسا ... » has no grammatical position; it is a causal clause.
And the clause: «آتاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
And the clause: «سيجعل اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(4) أولات: feminine of: أولو – and أولي – and see verse (179) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
(6) وجدكم: a maṣdar of وجد fī al-māl in the sense of "became wealthy"; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, and the fāʾ may also take fatḥa or kasra.

* Benefits:
The ʿidda of the divorced woman and its rulings.
The woman observing a revocable ʿidda is entitled to maintenance and lodging from the husband for as long as she is in the ʿidda. As for the woman observing an irrevocable (bāʾin) ʿidda, by khulʿ, by the triple divorce, or by liʿān, she is entitled to lodging, whether pregnant or not pregnant, according to most scholars. Ibn ʿAbbās said: she has no lodging unless she is pregnant; and Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī and al-Shāfiʿī said: she has no maintenance unless she is pregnant, which is the apparent meaning of the noble verse. [Translator's note: Ibn ʿAbbās appears twice in the source, with two different opinions, and "al-Ḥasan al-Shaʿbī" is written as one name; translated as written.] As for the woman observing an ʿidda after intercourse by mistake (shubha), or whose marriage has been annulled for a defect or by option on emancipation, she has neither lodging nor maintenance even if she is pregnant. As for the woman observing an ʿidda for the death of her husband, she has no maintenance according to most scholars; as for lodging, there are two opinions. The first: she has no lodging, and this is one of the two opinions of al-Shāfiʿī and of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿĀʾisha, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḥasan and Abū Ḥanīfa. The second: she has lodging, and this is the opinion of ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, Mālik, al-Thawrī, Aḥmad and Isḥāq. Know that divorce during menstruation and postpartum bleeding is an innovation (bidʿa), as is divorce in a period of purity in which he had intercourse with her. The sunna divorce is that he divorces her in a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her. This applies to a woman whose ʿidda is by menstrual periods (aqrāʾ). But if he divorces a woman with whom the marriage was not consummated during menstruation, or a young girl who has not yet menstruated, or a woman past menstruation after having had intercourse with her, or divorces a pregnant woman after having had intercourse with her, or divorces a woman who has not seen blood, there is no blame in that; and as for khulʿ during menstruation or in a period of purity in which he had intercourse with her, there is likewise no blame in it.
Divorce is the last measure to which the husband resorts, after all attempts at reconciliation have failed.
On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most hateful of lawful things to Allah is divorce."
And on the authority of Thawbān that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a pressing reason, the scent of Paradise is forbidden to her."
- The jussive-governing lām (the lām of command)..
It is the lām set for requesting, and its vowel is kasra; making it sākin after the fāʾ and the wāw is more frequent than vowelling it, as in the saying of the Exalted: (فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي); and it may be made sākin after ثمّ: (ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ). There is no difference, in the lām of request requiring the jussive, between the request being a command, as in the saying of the Exalted: (لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ), or a supplication: (لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ), or a plea, as when you say to one who is your equal "let so-and-so do such-and-such", if you do not intend to assert superiority over him. Likewise if it is turned from request to something else, as the one by which it and its accompanying verb are meant as a statement, as in the saying of the Exalted: (مَنْ كانَ فِي الضَّلالَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ مَدًّا), i.e. "so the Merciful extends (fa-yamudd)"; or a threat: (وَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ). As for the saying of the Exalted: (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا), both lāms may be the lām of reason, in which case what follows them is accusative, or the lām of threat, in which case it is jussive. The entry of the lām upon a verb of the first person (speaker) is rare, as in the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: (قوموا فلأصل لكم), and the saying of the Exalted: وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ. The lām may be deleted in poetry while its effect remains, as in the poet's words:
محمد تفد نفسك كل نفس ... إذا ما خفت من شيء تبالا
(O Muḥammad, let your soul ransom every soul, whenever you fear any harm.)
i.e. لتفد. And التبال is الوبال, meaning destruction.

safi-cedvel:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (كأيّن) a noun of indefinite number (kināya), indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (من قرية) tamyīz (specification). (عن أمر) attached to (عتت). (الفاء) conjunction. (حسابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, and likewise (عذابا)..
Clause: «كأيّن من قرية ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «عتت ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of كأيّن.
And the clause: «حاسبناها ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause عتت.
And the clause: «عذّبناها ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause عتت.
9- (الفاء) conjunction. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) – or resumptive..
And the clause: «ذاقت ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause عذّبناها.
And the clause: «كان عاقبة أمرها خسرا» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl, with an implied قد.

* Morphology:
(عتت): it contains an iʿlāl by deletion as in عتوا.. see verse (77) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
(خسرا): a samāʿī maṣdar (heard from the Arabs) of the triliteral خسر; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn. There are other maṣdars of the verb: خسر with fatḥa then sukūn, خسر with two ḍammas, خسار with fatḥa on the khāʾ, خسارة with fatḥa on the khāʾ, and خسران with ḍamma on the khāʾ and sukūn on the sīn..

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical figurative usage): in the saying of the Exalted وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّها.
The relation of this majāz is locality (maḥalliyya), from naming the place and intending what is in it.

safi-cedvel:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم) attached to (أعدّ). (الفاء) links to the apodosis of an implied condition. (أولي) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ. (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative, ʿaṭf bayān to أولي – or a badal from it. (قد) a particle of certainty. (إليكم) attached to (أنزل).
Clause: «أعدّ اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption confirming the content of what precedes.
And the clause: «اتّقوا ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if Allah has prepared punishment for whoever rebels against His command, then fear Him".
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «أنزل اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
11- (رسولا) a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "He sent a messenger" [Note: It may be a badal from (ذكرا), or an object of the maṣdar (ذكرا), or an object of an omitted verb in the sense of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "Adhere to ..."]. (عليكم) attached to (يتلو). (اللام) of reason. (يخرج) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (من الظلمات) attached to (يخرج), and likewise (إلى النور). (الواو) resumptive..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرج..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزل), or to (يتلو).
(من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (باللَّه) attached to (يؤمن). (يعمل) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to the protasis by the wāw. (صالحا) a direct object, accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, the direct object being implied]. (من تحتها) attached to (تجري) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار] with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath its trees". (خالدين) a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (يدخله), where the wording of (من) is observed in it. (فيها) attached to (خالدين), and likewise (أبدا), an adverb of time. (قد) a particle of certainty. (له) attached to a ḥāl from (رزقا) [Note: an adjective that has been placed before the noun it describes].
And the clause: «يتلو ... » is in the position of accusative, an adjective of (رسولا).
And the clause: «يخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «آمنوا ... (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «من يؤمن ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «يؤمن باللَّه ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together].
And the clause: «يعمل ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يؤمن.
And the clause: «يدخله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of accusative, an adjective of جنّات.
And the clause: «قد أحسن اللَّه ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (يدخله).
12- (الواو) conjunction. (من الأرض) attached to a ḥāl from (مثلهنّ), which is conjoined to سبع سموات [Note: It is also permissible that (مثلهنّ) be a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and He created their like from the earth", the conjunction then being a conjunction of clauses]. (بينهنّ) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يتنزّل). (لتعلموا) like ليخرج. (على كلّ) attached to the khabar (قدير). (الواو) conjunction. (بكل) attached to (أحاط) [Note: or attached to (علما)]. (علما) a tamyīz converted from the fāʿil, i.e.: "the knowledge of Allah has encompassed everything".
And the clause: «اللَّه الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «يتنزّل الأمر ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from سبع سموات, or from السموات والأرض.
And the clause: «تعلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تعلموا.) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I inform you of that".
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ اللَّه على كلّ شيء قدير) is in the position of accusative, standing in the place of the two objects of تعلموا.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله قد أحاط..) is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the last interpreted maṣdar.
And the clause: «قد أحاط ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of أنّ.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of the Exalted لِيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ. Here He, glorified and exalted, likened disbelief to darkness, then omitted the thing likened and retained the thing likened to; and likened faith to light, again omitting the thing likened and retaining the thing likened to.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it is an address to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the plural form, as a mark of honour, as in his saying:
4271 - فإنْ شِئْتِ حَرَّمْتُ النساءَ سواكمُ ... وإن شِئْتِ لم أَطْعَمْ نُقاخاً ولا بَرْدا
(If you wish, I will forbid women other than you; and if you wish, I will not taste cool sweet water, nor sleep.)
The second is that it is an address to him and to his community, the implied form being: "O Prophet, and your community, when you divorce", with the conjoined element omitted because what comes after indicates it, as in his saying:
4272 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إذا حَذْفَتْه رِجْلُها. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(... when her foot flung it...)
that is, "and her hand"; and this was given in Sūrat al-Naḥl at {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81]. The third is that it is an address to his community only, after calling him, peace be upon him, and this is a variation of address (talwīn al-khiṭāb): He addressed his community after He had addressed him. The fourth is that it is on the basis of an implied "say", that is: "O Prophet, say to your community: when you divorce." The fifth: al-Zamakhsharī said: "He singled out the Prophet ﷺ for the vocative and generalized in the address, because the Prophet is the leader of his community and their model, as one says to the chief of a people and their elder: 'O so-and-so, do such-and-such,' having regard to his precedence and showing his headship," in fine words; and this is the meaning of the third view, which I gave earlier.
And His saying {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ} means: "when you intend", like His saying {إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصلاة} [al-Māʾida: 6] and {فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ القرآن} [al-Naḥl: 98]; and the verification of that has been given.
His saying: {لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "facing their ʿidda (waiting period), as you say «أتيتُه لِلَيْلَةٍ بَقِيَتْ من المحرَّم», that is, 'facing it'; and in the reading of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «في قُبُل عِدَّتِهِنَّ»." End. The Shaykh took issue with him over his implying, for the ḥāl to which the preposition is attached, a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ), and said: "When a preposition and its genitive noun occurs as a ḥāl, it is attached only to an unspecified being." In his objection there is room for doubt, because al-Zamakhsharī did not make the preposition and its genitive noun a ḥāl, but made it attached to an omitted element which the meaning of the speech indicates. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ», that is, at the first moment at which they are counted for them, while they are at the beginning of the period of purity (qubul al-ṭuhr)." This is, on his part, an explanation of meaning and not an explanation of i'rāb. The Shaykh said: "It is on an omitted muḍāf, that is, «لاستقبالِ عِدَّتِهِن», and the lām is for fixing a time, like «لَقِيْتُه لِلَيْلَةٍ بَقِيَتْ مِنْ شهرِ كذا»." End. On this the lām is attached to «طَلِّقُوهن».
His saying: {لَعَلَّ الله}: this clause is resumptive, with no connection between it and what precedes, because the grammarians did not count it among the suspending particles (muʿallaqāt). The Shaykh held it to be among those that ought to be counted among them, and established that in His saying {وَإِنْ أَدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ لَّكُمْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 111]; its treatment is to be sought there.

semin-durr:2-2.t: The majority read {أَجَلَهُنَّ}, because the term, as such, is one, even if its kinds differ in relation to the women observing a waiting period. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Sīrīn read «آجالَهُنَّ», a broken plural, taking into account that the term of this one is other than the term of that one.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ}: Ḥafṣ read «بالغُ» without tanwīn, «أمرِه» being the muḍāf ilayhi, for lightness. The others read it with tanwīn and the accusative, which is the original, contrary to the Shaykh. Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, read «بالغٌ أمرُه» with tanwīn on «بالغٌ» and «أَمْرُه» nominative, and there are two possibilities in it. The first is that «بالغٌ» is a fronted khabar and «أمْرُه» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ». The second is that «بالغٌ» is the khabar of «إنَّ» and «أَمْرُه» is its agent. Al-Mufaḍḍal read «بالغاً» in the accusative and «أَمْرُه» in the nominative. There are two possibilities in it, the clearer of which, al-Zamakhsharī's explanation, is that «بالغاً» is accusative as a ḥāl, and {قَدْ جَعَلَ الله} is the khabar of «إنَّ», its implied form being: "Allah has set for everything a measure, its command reaching [its end]." The second is that it is on the dialect of those who put both the noun and the khabar of it in the accusative, as in his saying:
4273 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . إنَّ حُرَّاسَنا أُسْدا
(... indeed our guards are lions.)
and «قد جَعَل» is resumptive, as in the well-known reading. As for the one who put «أَمْرُه» in the nominative, the object of «بالغ» is omitted, its implied form being: "what He wills". Jināḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read «قَدَرا» with fatḥa on the dāl.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {واللائي يَئِسْنَ}: the disagreement about it has already been given. Abū ʿAmr reads here «واللايْ يَئِسْنَ» with clear pronunciation (iẓhār), whereas his rule in the like of it is assimilation (idghām); except that, since the yāʾ in his view is incidental, being a substitute for a hamza, it is as though two like letters had not met. Moreover its quiescence is incidental, so it is as though the yāʾ of «اللاي» were vowelled, and a letter, as long as it is vowelled, is not assimilated into another. He read «يَئِسْنَ» as a past verb; «يَيْئَسْنَ» was also read, as an imperfect. And «مِنْ المحيض مِنْ نسائكم»: the first «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), attached to the verb before it, and the second is for clarification, attached to an omitted element. «اللائي» is a mubtadaʾ, «فعِدَّتُهُنَّ» is a second mubtadaʾ, «وثلاثةُ أشهر» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of the first; the condition is parenthetical, and its apodosis is omitted. It is also possible that «إنِ ارْتَبْتُم» has as its apodosis {فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاَثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ}, the conditional clause being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. What the doubt is attached to is omitted; it was said that its implied form is: "if you doubt whether she has reached the age of despair or not, owing to the possibility of a pregnancy appearing, even though her blood has stopped." It was also said: "if you doubt about the blood of those who have reached the age of despair, whether it is menstrual blood or irregular bleeding." And if this is the waiting period of those about whom there is doubt, then those about whom there is no doubt are more deserving of it. The most strange of what was said is that «إنْ ارتَبْتُم» is in the sense of "if you are certain", so it would be one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād).
His saying: {واللائي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ}: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. They implied a clause like the first, that is: "their waiting period is also three months"; the better is to imply a single word, that is: "likewise", or "like them". And if it were said that it is conjoined to «اللائي يَئِسْنَ» as a conjunction of single words, and the khabar given for all of them by His saying «فعِدَّتُهنَّ», that would be a fine view; the most that can be said against it is the placing of the khabar between the mubtadaʾ and what is conjoined to it. This is the apparent meaning of the Shaykh's saying: {واللائي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ} is conjoined to «واللائي يَئِسْن», so its i'rāb as a mubtadaʾ is like the i'rāb of «واللائي».
His saying: {وَأُوْلاَتُ الأحمال}: a mubtadaʾ, and «أَجَلُهُنَّ» a second mubtadaʾ, and «أن يَضَعْن» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of the first, that is, "the delivery of their burden". It is also possible that «أَجلُهنَّ» is a badal ishtimāl (inclusion substitute) from «أُولات», and «أنْ يضعن» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The majority read «حَمْلهنَّ» in the singular; al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «آجالُهُنَّ», a broken plural.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {وَيُعْظِمْ}: this is the reading of the majority, the imperfect of أَعْظَمَ; Ibn Miqsam read «يُعَظِّمْ» with shadda, the imperfect of عَظَّم with shadda. Al-Aʿmash read «نُعْظِم», the imperfect of أَعْظم, which is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person to the first.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم}: there are two possibilities. The first is that «مِنْ» is partitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What is partitioned is omitted; its meaning is: house them in a place from where you dwell, that is, part of the place of your dwelling, as in the saying of the Exalted: {يَغُضُّواْ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ} [al-Nūr: 30], that is, part of their sight. Qatāda said: 'If there is only one house, let him house her in part of its sides.'" The second is that it is for the beginning of the extent, as al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ said. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning: take steps to house them in the way in which you house yourselves. His saying «مِنْ وُجْدِكم» indicates this, الوُجْد being wealth."
His saying: {مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is a badal from His saying «مِنْ حيثُ» with repetition of the governor, and Abū l-Baqāʾ held this, as if it were said: "house them from your means." The second is that it is an ʿaṭf bayān of His saying {مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم}, and al-Zamakhsharī held this, for he said, after parsing «مِنْ حيث» as partitive as above: "If you ask: and what of His saying «مِنْ وُجْدِكم»? I say: it is an ʿaṭf bayān of His saying {مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم} and an explanation of it, as if it were said: house them in a place among your dwellings, of what you can afford. الوُجْد is capacity and ability." The Shaykh took issue with him, saying that repetition of the governor is not known in ʿaṭf bayān; it is known only in the badal, and for that reason Abū l-Baqāʾ parsed it as a badal. The majority read «وُجْدِكم» with ḍamma on the wāw; al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and Abū Ḥaywa with fatḥa; al-Fayyāḍ ibn Ghazwān, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn and Yaʿqūb with kasra, which are dialects of one meaning. And الوَجْد with fatḥa on the wāw is also grief, love and anger.
His saying: {وَأْتَمِرُواْ}: ifʿalū from الأَمْر. One says: ايتَمَرَ القومُ and تآمروا, that is, they commanded one another. Al-Kisāʾī said: ائتمروا means "they consulted one another", and he recited the saying of the Exalted {إِنَّ الملأ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 20], and recited the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4274 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ويَعْدُوْ على المَرْءِ ما يَأَتْمِرْ
(... and what a man plans turns upon him.)
His saying: {فَسَتُرْضِعُ}: it was said: it is a khabar in the sense of a command. The pronoun in «له» refers to the father, as in His saying {فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ}, and the object is omitted because it is known, that is: "another woman will nurse the child for his father." The apparent sense is that it is a khabar in its ordinary sense.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {لِيُنفِقْ}: this is the reading of the majority, I mean kasra on the lām and jussive of the imperfect by it. Abū Muʿādh the reader reported «لِيُنْفِقَ» with the verb in the accusative, the lām being the lām of purpose (lām kay), the verb after it put in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ», and the preposition is then attached to an omitted element, that is: "We legislated that so that he may spend." The majority read «قُدِر» lightened; Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «قَدَّر» with shadda.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهَا}: it was made to imply the sense of "turned away", as if it were said: "it turned away because of its insolence." And His saying «فحاسَبْناها» to the end is all in the Hereafter, and He put it in the past wording because of its certainty. It was also said: the punishment is in this world, in which case it is taken in its literal sense. And «أعدَّ الله» is a repetition of the threat and an emphasis. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that «عَتَتْ» and what is conjoined to it be a ṣifa of «قريةٍ», and that the khabar of «كأيِّنْ» be the clause from His saying «أعدَّ اللَّهُ»; whereas on the first view the khabar is «عَتَتْ» and what is conjoined to it.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {الذين آمَنُواْ}: accusative by an implied «أَعْني» ("I mean"), as a clarification of the one addressed; or it is an ʿaṭf bayān for the one addressed, or a naʿt of it; and its being a badal is weak, because it cannot take the place of that for which it is a substitute.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {رَّسُولاً}: there are several possibilities. The first, which al-Zajjāj and al-Fārisī held, is that it is accusative by the maṣdar with tanwīn before it, because that dissolves into a maṣdar-particle and a verb, as if it were said: "that He mentioned a messenger"; and a maṣdar with tanwīn governs, as in the saying of the Exalted {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14] and in his saying: 4275 - بضَرْبٍ بالسيوفِ رؤوسَ قَوْمٍ ... أَزَلْنا هامَهُنَّ عن المَقيلِ
(By striking with swords the heads of a people, we removed their skulls from their resting place.)
The second is that the remembrance itself was made [the messenger] by way of exaggeration, and so a badal was made from it. The third is that it is a badal from it with an omitted muḍāf from the first, the implied form being: "He sent down one possessing a reminder, a messenger." The fourth is likewise, except that «رسولاً» is a naʿt of that omitted element. The fifth is that it is a badal from it with an omitted muḍāf from the second, that is: "a reminder, the reminder of a messenger." The sixth is that «رسولاً» is a naʿt of «ذِكْراً» with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "a reminder possessing a messenger", so «ذا رسول» is a naʿt of «ذِكْر». The seventh is that «رسولاً» is in the sense of "message" (risāla), so that «رسولاً» is an outright badal without interpretation, or a clarification according to those who allow it in indefinites, such as al-Fārisī; but his saying «يَتْلُو عليكم» makes this remote, because a message does not recite except figuratively. The eighth is that «رسولاً» is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "He sent a messenger", as what precedes indicates it. The ninth is that it is accusative as incitement (ighrāʾ), that is: "follow, and hold fast to, a messenger of this description."
The people differed about «رسولاً»: is he the Prophet ﷺ, or the Qur'ān itself, or Jibrīl? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He is Jibrīl, peace be upon him," made a badal from «ذِكْراً» because he is described as reciting the verses of Allah, so that his sending down is in the sense of sending down the Reminder, and therefore making him a badal from it is sound. The Shaykh said: "It is not sound, because of the difference in the referents in reality, and because it is neither a badal of part nor a badal of inclusion." End. What al-Zamakhsharī said was preceded in it by al-Kalbī. As for his objection to it, it is not necessarily so, because it is by exaggeration, until he was made the very Reminder, as its explanation was given earlier. «رسولٌ» was also read, with an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "he is a messenger."
His saying: {لِّيُخْرِجَ}: attached either to «أَنْزَل» or to «يَتْلو». The agent of «يُخْرِج» is either the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, who sends down, or the pronoun of the Messenger, or of the Reminder. And «مَنْ يُؤْمِنْ» is one of the places where the wording was regarded first, then the meaning second, then the wording last, as was given in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida. Some interpreted this verse [and said: His saying «خالدين» has no pronoun in it returning to «مَنْ»; it returns only to the object of «يُدْخِلْه», and «خالدين» is a ḥāl from it, and the governor in it is «يُدْخِلْه», not the verb of the condition]. This is the Shaykh's expression, and there is room for objection in it, because «خالدين» is a ḥāl from the object of «يُدْخِلْه» in the view of those who hold the first view; and the correction of the expression would be to say: a ḥāl from the second object of «يُدْخِلْه», which is «جناتٍ», and the abiding is in reality for their inhabitants; and in the view of the Basrans it should have been said «خالدين هم فيها», because the description is applied to other than the one to whom it belongs.
His saying: {قَدْ أَحْسَنَ الله}: a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خالدين», in which case it is nested.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {مِثْلَهُنَّ}: the majority read it in the accusative, and there are two possibilities. The first is that it is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «سَبْعَ سماواتٍ»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh objected, because it requires separation, by a preposition and its genitive noun, between the conjunction, which is a single letter, and the conjoined, and this is restricted to poetic necessity in the view of Abū ʿAlī. I say: this is parallel to His saying {آتِنَا فِي الدنيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخرة حَسَنَةً} [al-Baqara: 201] in the view of Ibn Mālik, and the treatment of this disagreement has been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, al-Nisāʾ and Hūd, at His saying {وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ الناس} [al-Nisāʾ: 58] and {وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ} [Hūd: 71].
The second is that it is accusative by an implied element after the wāw, that is: "and He created the like of them from the earth." The people differed about the likeness: it was said: like them in number. It was also said: in some attributes, since likeness is true by that; and the first is the well-known one. ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «مثلُهُنَّ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the preposition and its genitive noun before it as its khabar.
His saying {يَتَنَزَّلُ}: it may be resumptive, and it may be a naʿt of what precedes; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, and ʿĪsā, read «يُنَزِّل» with shadda, that is, Allah; «الأمر» is the direct object. The pronoun in «بينهنَّ» refers to the heavens and the earths in the view of the majority, or to the heavens and the earth in the view of those who say that it is a single earth.
His saying: {لتعلموا}: attached to «خَلَقَ» or to «يَتنزَّل». The majority read «لتعلَموا» in the second person, and some with a yāʾ of the third person.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ. . . (١))
His saying (إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ): it is said: the implied form is "say to your community: when you divorce". It is also said: the address is to him ﷺ and to others. (لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ), i.e. "at the beginning of what is counted for them [as their waiting period]", which is at the start of the period of purity.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَدْ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْرًا رَسُولًا يَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيِّنَاتٍ لِيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صَالِحًا يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقًا (١١))
His saying (رَسُولًا): there are several views on its accusative. The first: it is made accusative by ذِكْرًا [as a maṣdar], i.e. "He has sent down to you that He mentioned a messenger".
The second: it is a badal (substitute) from «ذِكْرًا», الرَّسُول being in the sense of الرِّسَالَة (the message). On this view «يَتْلُو» may be a naʿt (adjective), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the name of Allah the Exalted.
The third: the implied form is "a reminder: the honour of a messenger", or "a reminder: the mention of a messenger", what is meant by الذِّكْر being honour; the muḍāf ilayhi has been put in place of the muḍāf.
The fourth: it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and He sent a messenger".
His saying (قَدْ أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ): the clause is a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خَالِدِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ. . . (١٢))
His saying (مِثْلَهُنَّ): whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it, i.e. "and He created of the earth the like of them"; and whoever reads it in the nominative [مِثْلُهُنَّ] makes it a new sentence. And (يَتَنَزَّلُ) may be resumptive, and may be a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِ شَيْءٍ قَدْرًا (٣))
His saying (بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ) is read with tanwīn and the accusative [بَالِغٌ أَمْرَهُ], and with annexation and the genitive, the annexation being impure (ghayr maḥḍa). It is also read with tanwīn and the nominative [بَالِغٌ أَمْرُهُ], as the fāʿil (agent) of «بَالِغُ».
It is also said: أَمْرُهُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and بَالِغٌ its khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ وَأُولَاتُ الْأَحْمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ. . . (٤))
His saying (وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "their waiting period is likewise". And (أَجَلُهُنَّ) is a mubtadaʾ, «أَنْ يَضَعْنَ» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of أُولَاتُ. It is also possible for أَجَلُهُنَّ to be a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), i.e. "and the term of أُولَاتِ الْأَحْمَالِ".

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُمْ مِنْ وُجْدِكُمْ. . . (٦))
His saying (أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ): «مِنْ» here is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); the meaning is "arrange their lodging in the manner in which you lodge", and this is indicated by His saying (مِنْ وُجْدِكُمْ).
And الْوُجْدُ means wealth; [its wāw] may also take fatḥa and kasra. And مِنْ وُجْدِكُمْ is a badal (substitute) from «مِنْ حَيْثُ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṭalāq (Divorce)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾ — this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and the believers are included with him in the address. Its meaning is: "if you intend divorce," just as He said: ﴿إذا قُمْتُمْ إلى الصَّلاةِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 6], meaning: when you intend to stand for the prayer.

His saying: ﴿فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وأحْصُوا العِدَّةَ﴾ — the divorce of the Sunna (the one agreed upon, in the view of Mālik: that a man divorce his wife while she is in a state of purity, without intercourse, with a single pronouncement, then leave her, if he wishes to persist in separating from her, for three menstrual periods. When she enters the third menstruation he no longer has the right to take her back; but if he wishes and she wishes to renew a fresh marriage contract, that is open to them both.
